summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of atrial fibrillation and recent MRSA bacteremia was admitted for worsening headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, and shortness of breath. She had missed a dialysis session and presented with hypotension and low oxygen saturation. Initial concern for meningitis led to broad-spectrum antibiotics, though cryptococcal antigen and blood cultures were negative. Symptoms improved with hemodialysis and supportive care. Her headache was attributed to chronic pain and post-herpetic neuralgia, exacerbated by missed dialysis and medication changes. Warfarin was held due to elevated INR and restarted at a lower dose. Oral vancomycin for C. difficile was discontinued as diarrhea had resolved. She was discharged home with services, on a short course of oxycodone for pain, with follow-up planned for HIV adherence, eye care, and cardiac monitoring.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
